summary: A React Native library for JavaScript and native exception handling, graceful fallback flows, and crash-reporting integrations. It is designed for apps that need one place to register handlers, validate release-mode crash behavior, and forward failures to Sentry, Crashlytics, or a custom backend.
useCases: Install JavaScript and native exception handlers in one package
Show fallback UI or recovery flows for fatal JavaScript errors
Log or report native crash payloads to Sentry, Crashlytics, or a custom backend
Preserve an existing native handler with callPreviouslyDefinedHandler
Validate release-mode crash behavior with simulateNativeCrash
Migrate from react-native-exception-handler without changing the core JS flow
nonGoals: It does not make native crash handling equivalent to JavaScript exception handling
It does not guarantee restart-oriented recovery on iOS after a fatal native crash
It does not remove the need to run CocoaPods and rebuild native apps after installation
It does not make debug-mode crash behavior a reliable substitute for release-mode validation
constraints: Native crash handling is more limited than JavaScript exception handling
Debug behavior is not a reliable proxy for release behavior
iOS and Android native crash flows differ materially
Some integrations require chaining a previously defined native handler
simulateNativeCrash is for QA and release validation, not end-user flows

Check function signatures and option defaults

apiMap.name: setJSExceptionHandler(customHandler, allowedInDevMode)
apiMap.purpose: Registers the global JavaScript exception handler.
notes: Use for uncaught JavaScript exceptions before the app exits.
allowedInDevMode lets you opt into handler behavior during development.

apiMap.name: getJSExceptionHandler()
apiMap.purpose: Returns the currently registered JavaScript exception handler.
notes: Useful when you need to preserve or chain an existing JS handler.

apiMap.name: setNativeExceptionHandler(customErrorHandler, options)
notes: Prefer the options-object signature over the older positional form.
Keep native crash work minimal and validate behavior in release builds.

apiMap.name: getNativeExceptionHandler()
apiMap.purpose: Returns the currently registered native exception handler.
notes: Use when you need to preserve or inspect an existing native handler.

apiMap.name: simulateNativeCrash(crashType)
apiMap.purpose: Simulates a native crash for QA and release validation.
notes: Do not expose this through end-user flows.
Use a controlled test environment when validating destructive crash types.

coreOptions.name: forceAppToQuit
notes: Use with care if you are attempting advanced recovery flows.

coreOptions.name: callPreviouslyDefinedHandler
notes: Use when another SDK or native layer already installed a handler.
Relevant for Sentry, Crashlytics, or custom native crash pipelines.

common: JavaScript exceptions and native crashes are not interchangeable.
Release builds are the only reliable way to validate native crash behavior.
ios: Native crash recovery is more limited on iOS.
Do not assume a normal React Native UI flow is still safe after a fatal native crash.
android: Android offers more flexibility for restart-oriented recovery flows.
forceAppToQuit changes how advanced Android recovery attempts behave.

testingNotes: Use simulateNativeCrash for release validation, not as a production feature.
Test JavaScript handling and native crash handling separately.
Verify provider integrations end-to-end in the same environment you plan to ship.
If native results differ from expectations, compare debug and release behavior before changing handler logic.
